# ToolPick
> Needs-based AI tool finder. 82 tools, prices copied from official pricing pages; each tool has its own checked date (latest 2026-10-19). 'check site' means unverified.

## Categories
- [Video](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/best-ai-video-tools.html): best value Runway; free options CapCut, HeyGen, Synthesia
- [Writing](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/best-ai-writing-tools.html): best value Claude; free options ChatGPT, Google Gemini, Grammarly
- [Coding](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/best-ai-coding-tools.html): best value GitHub Copilot; free options GitHub Copilot, Windsurf, v0
- [Images](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/best-ai-images-tools.html): best value Leonardo; free options Leonardo, Krea, Ideogram
- [Audio](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/best-ai-audio-tools.html): best value ElevenLabs; free options ElevenLabs, Suno, Otter
- [Presentations](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/best-ai-presentations-tools.html): best value Pitch; free options Pitch, SlidesAI, Canva
- [AI Assistants](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/best-ai-assistants-tools.html): best value Le Chat (Mistral); free options ChatGPT, Claude, Google Gemini
- [Marketing & SEO](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/best-ai-marketing-tools.html): best value Buffer; free options Buffer
- [Research](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/best-ai-research-tools.html): best value Elicit; free options Consensus, Elicit, ResearchRabbit
- [Productivity & Meetings](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/best-ai-productivity-tools.html): best value Fireflies; free options Fireflies, Zapier, Superhuman
- [Chatbots & Agents](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/best-ai-agents-tools.html): best value Botpress; free options Botpress, Zapier Agents

## Refunds and cancelling (v52)
- [Can I get a refund? AI subscription refund and cancel rules](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/ai-refund-policies.html): 22 AI tools (Bolt, Canva, ChatGPT, Claude, Cursor, Descript, ElevenLabs, Fireflies, Gamma, GitHub Copilot, Grammarly, HeyGen, Ideogram, Jasper, Lovable, Midjourney, Notion AI, Otter, Perplexity, Runway, Suno, Synthesia): refund window and conditions (monthly/yearly), how to ask, exact cancel steps, cancel-notice deadlines, what you lose after cancelling, app-store note, official refund and cancel page links, read 2026-10-27. Checker params: ?tool=chatgpt&when=d7&bill=y (when = pre, h24, d2, d3, d7, d14, d30, old)
  - Bolt: No refunds. Bolt doesn't give refunds. Cancelling only stops the next charge.
  - Canva: Case by case. Case by case: Canva reviews every request but says most subscriptions aren't refundable.
  - ChatGPT: Refund window. Possible within 7 days of the charge, if the subscription is unused (their call).
  - Claude: Case by case. Case by case: only payments their Consumer Terms call refundable, or where the law requires.
  - Cursor: Refund window. Possible within 14 days of the charge, if you haven't used it that billing period.
  - Descript: Refund window. Possible within 48 hours of the charge.
  - ElevenLabs: Refund window. Possible within 14 days of the charge, if you haven't used any credits.
  - Fireflies: Refund window. Possible within 7 days of the charge, depending on how many meetings you logged.
  - Gamma: Refund window. Possible within 3 days of the charge when you first subscribe, only through support and under a credit limit.
  - GitHub Copilot: No refunds. GitHub Copilot doesn't give refunds. Cancelling only stops the next charge.
  - Grammarly: No refunds. Grammarly doesn't give refunds. Cancelling only stops the next charge.
  - HeyGen: Case by case. Case by case, within 15 days of the charge, less likely if you used a lot of credits.
  - Ideogram: No refunds. Ideogram doesn't give refunds. Cancelling only stops the next charge.
  - Jasper: Refund window. Possible within 7 days of the charge, after you cancel.
  - Lovable: No refunds. Lovable doesn't give refunds. Cancelling only stops the next charge.
  - Midjourney: Refund window. Only if you've used less than 20 GPU minutes in your account's whole lifetime (Fast, Turbo and Relax all count). No time limit is stated.
  - Notion AI: Refund window. Possible within 3 days (monthly) or 30 days (yearly) of the charge, asked from the owner or billing email.
  - Otter: No refunds. Otter doesn't give refunds. Cancelling only stops the next charge.
  - Perplexity: Refund window. Possible within 24 hours (monthly) or 3 days (yearly) of the charge, one refund per account.
  - Runway: Refund window. Possible within 30 days of the charge, if unused or close to unused (their call).
  - Suno: Case by case. Case by case: Suno decides. Their examples: a subscription with zero songs made is likely refunded, an accidental yearly payment may get a partial refund, “changed your mind” isn't.
  - Synthesia: No refunds. Synthesia doesn't give refunds. Cancelling only stops the next charge.

## AI data privacy (v54)
- [Does this AI train on my data?](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/ai-data-privacy.html): 21 AI tools: whether free/personal plans train on your content by default (yes / only if you allow / no / unclear), exact opt-out steps, team/business plan default, retention notes, official source links, read 2026-10-29. Checker params: ?tool=chatgpt&plan=business; filters ?f=n (doesn't train by default), ?f=o (opt-out available), ?f=b (business plans protected)
  - Canva: personal plans: Unclear — see policy; team/business: Protected by default. Personal accounts: Canva may use your content to train its AI depending on your Privacy Settings. The pages we read don't say whether that is on or off by default. Opt out: Profile picture → Your account → Privacy controls → switch off the AI training options. Source: https://www.canva.com/trust/privacy/
  - ChatGPT: personal plans: Trains by default; team/business: Protected by default. Free, Plus and Pro: OpenAI may use your chats to train its models unless you turn it off. Opt out: Settings → Data controls → turn off “Improve the model for everyone”. Or ask “Do not train on my content” in OpenAI's Privacy Portal. Temporary chats aren't used for training. Source: https://help.openai.com/en/articles/5722486-how-your-data-is-used-to-improve-model-performance
  - Claude: personal plans: Only if you allow it; team/business: Protected by default. Free, Pro and Max: Anthropic uses your chats and coding sessions for training only if you allow it in your privacy settings (also if you send feedback, or a chat is flagged for safety review). Opt out: Settings → Privacy → switch off the model-improvement toggle (“Help improve Claude”). Incognito chats are never used for training. Source: https://privacy.claude.com/en/articles/10023580-is-my-data-used-for-model-training
  - Cursor: personal plans: Unclear — see policy; team/business: Admin decides. With Privacy Mode off, Cursor may store and use your code, prompts and editor actions to train its models. Cursor's pages don't say whether Privacy Mode starts on or off for individual plans. Opt out: Turn on Privacy Mode in Cursor's settings (free and paid plans). With it on, your code isn't trained on and isn't kept. Source: https://cursor.com/data-use
  - Descript: personal plans: Only if you allow it; team/business: Protected by default. You're asked when you sign up (“Share data with Descript”). Descript's AI models in use today use no user data; only opted-in data goes into research. Opt out: App Settings (Ctrl/Cmd + ,) → Profile → “Share data with Descript” → switch it off. Source: https://help.descript.com/account-and-app-settings/data-privacy
  - ElevenLabs: personal plans: Trains by default; team/business: Protected by default. Free and paid individual plans: ElevenLabs uses some of the data you give it to improve its audio models for everyone. Opt out: Profile icon → Terms and privacy → Data use → turn off “Improve the models for everyone” → Update your choice. Source: https://elevenlabs.io/docs/help-center/legal/is-my-data-used-to-improve-eleven-labs-ai-models
  - Fathom: personal plans: Trains by default; team/business: Admin decides. Fathom uses de-identified customer data to improve its own AI models. The AI companies it uses can't train on your data. Opt out: Opt out in My Settings (Fathom's page doesn't name the exact switch). Source: https://help.fathom.video/en/articles/296512
  - Fireflies: personal plans: Doesn't train by default; team/business: Protected by default. Meeting audio, video, transcripts and summaries are never used to train AI models, by Fireflies or its vendors. Source: https://guide.fireflies.ai/articles/2154538358-policy-on-keeping-information-safe
  - Gamma: personal plans: Trains by default; team/business: Protected by default. Free, Plus, Pro and Ultra: your content can be used to train Gamma's AI by default. Opt out: Your avatar → Settings → Data Controls → turn off AI training. Source: https://help.gamma.app/en/articles/12281928-does-gamma-use-my-content-to-train-its-ai-features
  - GitHub Copilot: personal plans: Trains by default; team/business: Protected by default. Copilot Free, Pro, Pro+ and Max: since April 24, 2026 GitHub may use your prompts, suggestions and the code Copilot sees to train AI models unless you opt out. Opt out: Profile picture → Copilot settings → “Allow GitHub to use my data for AI model training” → Disabled. Source: https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/manage-your-account/manage-policies
  - Google Gemini: personal plans: Trains by default; team/business: Protected by default. Personal Google accounts: while Keep Activity is on, Google uses your Gemini activity to improve its services, including training generative AI models, and human reviewers may read some chats. Opt out: Open Gemini Apps Activity → turn off Keep Activity. Or use a temporary chat. Chats are still kept for 72 hours. Source: https://support.google.com/gemini/answer/13594961
  - Grammarly: personal plans: Trains by default; team/business: Admin decides. Free, Premium and single-user Pro: “Product Improvement and Training” is on by default, so your text can be used to train Grammarly's models. Opt out: Go to account.grammarly.com/security/privacy → switch off “Product Improvement and Training”. Source: https://support.grammarly.com/hc/en-us/articles/25555503115277
  - Le Chat (Mistral): personal plans: Trains by default; team/business: Admin decides. Personal accounts (Mistral now calls the app Vibe): you're not opted out by default, so your chats can be used to train Mistral's models. Opt out: Web: Admin panel → Manage → Vibe → Privacy → turn off “Allow your interactions to be used to train our models”. Phone app: Settings → Data & Account Controls → untick “Enable data sharing”. Source: https://help.mistral.ai/en/articles/455207-can-i-opt-out-of-my-input-or-output-data-being-used-for-training
  - Lovable: personal plans: Trains by default; team/business: Protected by default. Free and Pro: since September 9, 2026 your data may be used to train Lovable's AI models. Data your app's own users enter isn't used. Opt out: Account settings → Preferences → AI model training → turn off “Use my Lovable content for model training”. Source: https://docs.lovable.dev/features/business/data-opt-out
  - Microsoft Copilot: personal plans: Doesn't train by default; team/business: Protected by default. New Copilot app (from August 18, 2026), personal account: your prompts, responses and files aren't used to train foundation models. Opt out: Nothing to switch off in the new app. Still on the older app? Profile icon → your name → Privacy → turn off “Training on conversation activity” and “Training on voice conversations”. Source: https://support.microsoft.com/en-us/privacy/microsoft-copilot/activity-history
  - Notion AI: personal plans: Doesn't train by default; team/business: Protected by default. Every plan: by default neither Notion nor its AI providers use your workspace content to train models. Source: https://www.notion.com/help/notion-ai-security-practices
  - Otter: personal plans: Trains by default; team/business: Unclear — see policy. Otter trains its own speech models on de-identified recordings and transcripts. Its outside AI providers don't train on your data. Opt out: Account Settings → Meetings → Feedback and Training → choose “Don't allow sharing”. Otter says future conversations then won't be used for training. Source: https://otter.ai/privacy-security
  - Perplexity: personal plans: Trains by default; team/business: Protected by default. Free, Pro and Max: “AI Data Retention” is on by default, so your data can be used to improve Perplexity's AI models. Opt out: Account settings → Preferences → turn off “AI data retention”. It only applies from then on. Source: https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/11564572-data-collection-at-perplexity
  - Runway: personal plans: Trains, no opt-out found; team/business: Unclear — see policy. Runway's Terms of Use say your inputs and outputs may be used to train and improve its AI models. We found no opt-out setting on its official pages. Source: https://runway.com/terms-of-use
  - Synthesia: personal plans: Doesn't train by default; team/business: Protected by default. Synthesia doesn't use your inputs or outputs to pre-train its AI. It only fine-tunes (for example a custom avatar) when you ask in writing. Source: https://www.synthesia.io/legal/ai-governance-practices
  - Zapier: personal plans: Doesn't train by default; team/business: Protected by default. Every plan: Zapier doesn't train on the data that runs through your workflows. It may learn from how workflows are built (the structure, not the contents). Opt out: To stop the structure learning too, use the opt-out form linked on Zapier's security page. Source: https://zapier.com/security-compliance
  - Left out: Midjourney (its privacy policy mentions training data but doesn't plainly say whether your prompts and images train its models, or how to opt out)
  - Left out: Jasper (its trust page only says your data isn't used to train outside AI models; it doesn't say what Jasper itself does)

## AI budget planner (v55)
- [Build my AI stack under $X/mo](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/ai-budget-planner.html): pick up to 6 of 36 jobs and a monthly budget; returns the best mix of ToolPick's top-3 picks per job that fits (paid #1 > #2 > #3 > confirmed free plan > none; a tool shared across jobs is paid once), the next upgrade and a price ladder. Params: ?jobs=youtube-shorts,meeting-notes&b=20&bill=y (yearly billing OK). Entry prices read on official pricing pages 2026-10-30:

## Real cost of AI images (v56)
- [AI image cost calculator](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/ai-image-cost.html): images per month you keep x tries per keeper -> cheapest plan (plan, plan + top-ups where priced, or unlimited slow mode if ?slow=1) and $ per kept image for Midjourney, Ideogram, Recraft, Krea; same-model 'cheaper' verdicts only (Ideogram 4.0 Turbo, Recraft V4.1 Flash). Params: ?n=100&t=4&slow=1&m=midjourney:0,ideogram:0,recraft:1,krea:5. Official pages checked 2026-10-31:
  - Midjourney (https://docs.midjourney.com/hc/en-us/articles/27870484040333-Comparing-Midjourney-Plans): Basic $10/mo 200 GPU minutes; Standard $30/mo 900 GPU minutes + unlimited slow; Pro $60/mo 1,800 GPU minutes + unlimited slow; Mega $120/mo 3,600 GPU minutes + unlimited slow. Per image: Standard image (SD) 0.2 GPU minutes; HD image 0.325 GPU minutes. Extra: extra Fast GPU time at $4 an hour (we round up to whole hours).
  - Ideogram (https://ideogram.ai/pricing): Pay as you go $0/mo 0 credits; Plus $20/mo 2,400 credits + unlimited slow; Pro $60/mo 7,500 credits + unlimited slow. Per image: Ideogram 4.0 (2K), Turbo 3 credits; Ideogram 4.0 (2K), Balanced 6 credits; Ideogram 4.0 (2K), Quality 10 credits; Ideogram 4.5, Low 3 credits; Ideogram 4.5, Medium 6 credits; Ideogram 4.5, High 10 credits; Ideogram 3.0, Default 6 credits. Extra: pay as you go at 1¢ per credit (no plan; minimum purchase not shown).
  - Recraft (https://www.recraft.ai/pricing): Basic $12/mo 1,000 credits; Pro $20/mo 2,000 credits. Per image: Recraft V4.1 2 credits; Recraft V4.1 Flash 1 credits; Recraft V4.1 Pro 10 credits; Recraft V4.1 Vector 4 credits; Recraft V4.1 Pro Vector 12 credits. Extra: top-up packs of 200 credits for $2.
  - Krea (https://www.krea.ai/pricing): Basic $9/mo 5,000 units; Pro $35/mo 20,000 units; Max $105/mo 60,000 units. Per image: Krea 2 Turbo 2 units; Krea 3 18 units; Flux.1 Dev 3.33 units; Nano Banana 2 (1K) 44.4 units; Ideogram 4.0, Turbo (resolution not stated) 22.2 units; Recraft V4.1 Flash 5.19 units; Seedream 4.5 29.6 units. Extra: compute packs (price needs sign-in, so not used).
  - Left out: Leonardo (its pricing page doesn't say how many tokens an image uses (it depends on the model and settings), so we can't turn 8,500 tokens into images)
  - Left out: Magnific (plans mix yearly credit pools and “unlimited” models that change by plan and billing period, so there's no clear monthly image count to compare)
  - Left out: ChatGPT (its pricing page only says “Limited”, “More” or “Unlimited” image creation, with no number)
  - Left out: Canva (its pricing page describes AI as a shared allowance (“10x more AI than Canva Free”) with no image count)
  - Left out: Photoroom (it edits product photos (backgrounds, scenes) rather than selling image-generation credits)


## My AI costs
- [My AI costs](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/my-ai-costs.html): one page with tabs for the subscription audit, watchlist, renewal reminders, cost calculator, and real cost of AI video and voice. Old URLs redirect to the matching #tab.

## Smart search (v45)
- [Finder](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/?q=voiceover%20under%20%2410): type a whole sentence. It reads the job, a budget ("under $10", "$120/year"), team size ("team of 5": per-seat totals only where the verified entry price is per seat), billing ("no annual plan"), "free", "cheap", and tool names: "cheaper than ChatGPT" (same main job, same billing, like-for-like tiers), "like ElevenLabs but free", "ChatGPT vs Claude" (links the full comparison). Shareable: https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/?q=cheaper%20than%20ChatGPT

## Tools directory (v53)
- [Browse all AI tools](https://toolpick-ai.vercel.app/tools.html): search all 82 tools by name or job (e.g. /tools.html?q=voiceover), filter by what each tool does (?job=text-to-speech, from each tool's own site), category (?category=video), real free plan (?free=yes), verified starting price (?price=u10), billing (?billing=monthly), Best Value picks (?bv=1); card or table view (?view=table); compare up to 3. Prices from official pricing pages with checked dates.
